skill.name: agent-memory
skill.description: Store, search, update, and organize persistent Markdown memories for agent work across conversations.
skill.summary: Maintain a searchable local memory folder for useful project knowledge and decisions.
skill.author: yamadashy

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks, fenced examples, or fixed-path shell snippets used to document local memory operations. No prompt injection, network access, credential access, or malicious command construction was found, but persistent proactive memory storage creates a privacy risk if sensitive information is saved.

remediation.issue: Persistent memories can retain sensitive project or user information.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to avoid storing secrets, credentials, personal data, private keys, tokens, and confidential customer content.

remediation.issue: Memory file paths are described with placeholders but no path validation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to use kebab-case names only and keep all writes and deletes inside the memories directory.

remediation.issue: Deletion guidance uses shell commands that could remove the wrong path if adapted carelessly.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation of the exact memory file path before deleting or reorganizing saved memories.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Local Memory May Capture Sensitive Context
semantic_findings.description: The skill encourages proactive saving of useful findings into a persistent memory directory. Without explicit guidance to avoid secrets or personal data, agents could retain sensitive project or user context across sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly tells agents to save durable memories proactively and write useful context for future use. The risk is contextual because the content depends on what agents choose to store.

content.value_statement: Important project details are easy to lose between AI sessions. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured local memory workflow.
actual_capabilities: Creates Markdown memory files with required summary frontmatter.
Organizes memories into category folders using kebab-case names.
Searches memory summaries, tags, and full text with ripgrep.
Updates, deletes, consolidates, and reorganizes outdated memories.
Uses a gitignored memories directory for local agent notes.
limitations: It stores memories as local files, not in a shared remote database.
It relies on the agent to choose useful and safe content to save.
It does not provide encryption, access control, or retention policies.
It requires shell and filesystem access for the documented workflow.

use_cases.title: Preserve Debugging Knowledge
use_cases.description: Save root causes, fixes, and related files after difficult investigations so later sessions can recover context quickly.

use_cases.title: Track Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Record decisions, rationale, and follow-up notes in a searchable project memory folder.

use_cases.title: Organize Research Notes
use_cases.description: Group findings from repeated research tasks into clear categories with searchable summaries and tags.

prompt_templates.title: Save A Simple Memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request to store one useful fact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Remember this project fact: [fact]. Save it with a clear summary and the right category.

prompt_templates.title: Recall Related Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Find existing memory before starting related work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check your memories for anything related to [topic]. Summarize the most relevant notes before we continue.

prompt_templates.title: Update Existing Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Refresh a memory after information changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the saved memory about [topic] with this new information: [details]. Keep the summary current.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate A Memory Area
prompt_templates.prompt: Review memories about [area]. Merge duplicates, remove outdated notes, and keep a concise searchable structure.

output_examples.input: Remember that our file importer fails on very large CSV files because of worker memory limits.
output_examples.output: Saved a memory in a file-processing category with a summary about the large CSV worker memory limit.

output_examples.input: What do your notes say about the authentication migration?
output_examples.output: Found relevant memory summaries, then reported the migration decision, current status, and files to review.

output_examples.input: Clean up the old notes about the deprecated export service.
output_examples.output: Reviewed matching memories, removed obsolete entries, and kept the current replacement-service note.

best_practices: Save only durable context that will help future work.
Write summaries that clearly state whether the full memory is worth reading.
Review memories periodically to remove outdated or sensitive content.
anti_patterns: Do not store secrets, credentials, tokens, or private customer data.
Do not save every conversation detail without clear future value.
Do not delete or reorganize memories without checking the exact target files.

faq.question: Where does the skill store memories?
faq.answer: It stores Markdown files under the skill memory directory in the local workspace.

faq.question: Can memories be searched?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow uses ripgrep to search summaries, tags, and full text.

faq.question: Does this sync memories across machines?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes local file storage and does not include remote sync.

faq.question: What should each memory include?
faq.answer: Each memory should include frontmatter with a concise summary and a created date.

faq.question: Can memories be updated or deleted?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes workflows to update, delete, consolidate, and reorganize memories.

faq.question: Is it safe to store sensitive information?
faq.answer: No. Avoid storing secrets, credentials, personal data, and confidential content.
